options.metric: Number of eligible crash rows by weekday of crash_date, pooled across 2013–2025
options.denominator: No rate denominator; absolute count of one-row-per-crash police-reported records with crash_date in 2013–2025
options.grouping: Weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.reason: Absolute counts give a direct picture of how the full-period collection of reported crash records is distributed across weekdays.
options.answer: Of 2,132,218 eligible police-reported crash records, weekday counts from Monday through Sunday are 304,518, 313,488, 311,111, 318,376, 338,800, 288,381, and 257,544, respectively, so Friday has the most and Sunday the fewest.
options.interpretation: This answers the full-period weekday distribution question as pooled counts of one-row-per-crash police-reported records dated from January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2025, grouped Monday through Sunday; Friday has the most rows and Sunday the fewest. Counts are a defensible direct measure of the recorded crash burden, but do not adjust for the number of calendar dates or travel exposure, and this pooled chart does not show separate weekday patterns by year. Annual eligible row counts in 2013–2025 are 203,742, 206,046, 217,708, 229,833, 231,007, 231,564, 211,486, 112,918, 110,558, 103,887, 96,607, 91,316, and 85,546; these changing volumes mean years with more records contribute more to pooled weekday counts, so the chart is not a year-to-year comparison. The date check found 0 NULL dates and no missing, unknown, impossible, or recognized sentinel dates in the selected population; 136,969 dated rows outside 2013–2025 were excluded, and all years had January 1 and December 31 boundary dates, so I retained every eligible row without an unknown-weekday group.

options.metric: Eligible crash-row count by weekday divided by all eligible crash rows, expressed as a percentage
options.denominator: All 2,132,218 police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date in 2013–2025
options.grouping: Weekday of crash_date, Monday through Sunday; each weekday count divided by the pooled eligible total
options.reason: Period-wide percentages show each weekday's contribution to all reported crashes without making the overall scale depend on the size of the file.
options.answer: The shares from Monday through Sunday are 14.28%, 14.70%, 14.59%, 14.93%, 15.89%, 13.52%, and 12.08%, respectively, with Friday the largest and Sunday the smallest.
options.interpretation: This answers the full-period weekday distribution question as the percentage of all one-row-per-crash police-reported records dated from January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2025, grouped Monday through Sunday; Friday accounts for the largest share and Sunday the smallest. Shares are a defensible compositional measure because each weekday's count is divided by the same pooled denominator of 2,132,218 eligible records, but they do not adjust for calendar-day counts or travel exposure and the pooled chart does not show separate weekday patterns by year. Annual eligible row counts in 2013–2025 are 203,742, 206,046, 217,708, 229,833, 231,007, 231,564, 211,486, 112,918, 110,558, 103,887, 96,607, 91,316, and 85,546; this changing volume means years with more records contribute more to each pooled share, so the chart is not an annual comparison. The date check found 0 NULL dates and no missing, unknown, impossible, or recognized sentinel dates in the selected population; 136,969 dated rows outside 2013–2025 were excluded, and all years had January 1 and December 31 boundary dates, so I retained every eligible row without an unknown-weekday group.
